properties.name: color-interpolation

values.name: auto
values.description: The browser may interpolate in either the sRGB or the linearRGB color space.

values.name: sRGB
values.description: Interpolate in the sRGB color space. This is the initial value.

values.name: linearRGB
values.description: Interpolate in the linearized RGB color space.

properties.description: Specifies the color space used for gradient interpolation, color animation and alpha compositing in SVG.

Defines a custom CSS function, called like a built-in one as `--name(arguments)`. Its body can declare local custom properties and returns the value of its `result` descriptor.

— *CSS Functions and Mixins Module*

Syntax: `@function <function-token> <function-parameter>#? ','? ) [ returns <css-type> ]? { <declaration-rule-list> }`
Matches elements that have a heading level, such as `<h1>`–`<h6>`. The functional form `:heading(2, 3)` matches only the listed levels.
Matches an element with `interestfor` while the user is showing interest in it, for example by hovering or focusing it.
Matches the target of an `interestfor` element while the user is showing interest in that element.
Matches the element that started the current navigation, such as the clicked link. It reflects `NavigateEvent.sourceElement`.
Matches scroll markers that come after the active one (the marker matching `:target-current`) in their scroll marker group.
Matches scroll markers that come before the active one (the marker matching `:target-current`) in their scroll marker group.

The ::field-content pseudo-element represents the portion of the input that contains the editable text.

— *CSS Form Control Styling Level 1*

The ::interest-button pseudo-element represents a button which, when pressed, shows interest in the originating element. This pseudo-element only exists on valid interest sources. (See interest-delay, :interest-source, and :interest-target for more discussion of this feature, and the HTML interestfor attribute.)

— *CSS Pseudo-Elements Module Level 4*

A browser-generated button that scrolls its scroll container. The argument picks the direction (`up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `block-start`, `block-end`, `inline-start`, `inline-end`, or `*` for all); the button appears once it has a `content` value.
Styles text matched by the browser's find-in-page feature. `::search-text:current` targets the active match.
Wraps the nested view transition groups of a captured element when `view-transition-group` nests them, so they can be clipped or styled together. Takes a view transition name.
